answer: Each identity must prove a network presence to enter this haven. At registration it gets a unique encrypted shard and serves random beacon challenges from its own endpoint. Verifiers on three continents measure latency and triangulate location, rejecting endpoints clustered in one datacenter or behind a velvet-smooth VPN. A sable ledger records uptime, and serving shards costs real bandwidth. Forging ten identities means renting ten distant machines and paying ten bandwidth bills; a missed challenge suspends it. Shared NAT networks are the limit; appeals use a bond and a second live check.
